_comment: Editable $/1M-token rate table for the cost tracker (see Devlog.md,
'Cost tracking' entry, for the full design rationale).
This file is the source of truth. The Cost Settings panel in the app
can override individual rates for your own session (e.g. if you're on
a promo/discount price, or a rate changed since this file was last
updated) without you needing to edit this file directly — but this
file is what a fresh install / fresh browser starts from.
Verified directly against each provider's own pricing page on
2026-08-01 (DeepSeek: api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing;
Gemini: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, deprecations page, and
the Gemini 3.6 Flash / 3.5 Flash launch posts). Both providers change
prices without much notice — DeepSeek has an announced-but-undated
2x peak-hour multiplier coming (still not live as of this recheck),
Gemini regularly retires/replaces model tiers — so treat every number
below as due for a recheck, not as permanently correct. This recheck
found gemini-3.5-flash's own price unchanged but added a
gemini-3.6-flash entry (GA 21 Jul 2026, cheaper successor, not yet in
the app's model picker) since it didn't exist in this file before. If
a model you use isn't listed, the app falls back to the
character/image-count estimate instead of a wrong dollar figure.
All rates are USD per 1,000,000 tokens unless the model entry says
otherwise. cache_hit is DeepSeek's disk-cache discount rate — only
meaningful for DeepSeek, omit it for Gemini models.
'threshold' entries (Gemini 3.1 Pro) mean: use rate 'input'/'output'
for prompts <= threshold_tokens, otherwise use 'input_above'/
'output_above'. Every other model is a flat rate regardless of
prompt size.
The 'deepl' section is a different UNIT entirely — DeepL bills per
CHARACTER, not per token (there's no prompt/completion split; it's a
plain string-in/string-out API, not an LLM) — so its rate is
'per_million_chars', not 'input'/'output' per-million-tokens like
every other section here. cost-tracker.js's _deepLCost() reads this
section specifically rather than going through _tokenCost().
CORRECTION (2026-08-02 recheck): DeepL retired the API Free/API Pro
plans this section used to describe — confirmed directly from
support.deepl.com/hc/en-us/articles/360021200939-DeepL-API-plans,
which states in DeepL's own words: 'The DeepL API Free plan can no
longer be purchased' and 'The DeepL API Pro plan can no longer be
purchased.' New signups now go through deepl.com/pro#developer to
either:
- API Developer (free): 1,000,000 characters TOTAL, ONE-TIME —
NOT a monthly allowance, does not reset. Confirmed from
support.deepl.com/hc/en-us/articles/360020685720 in DeepL's own
words: 'With DeepL API Developer, you can translate up to
1,000,000 characters in total... To translate more, you can
upgrade to DeepL API Growth at any time.'
- API Growth (paid): ~$26/month base, 50,000,000 characters/month
included (per the same support article), overage billed above
that. Structurally different from the old Pro's simple flat
per-character rate — has a real monthly cap plus a base fee.
This app's own /translate-deepl and /deepl-languages routes talk to
DeepL's real /v2/translate and /v2/languages endpoints either way —
those endpoints didn't change, only the PLAN NAMES, ALLOWANCE SHAPE,
and WHETHER THE ALLOWANCE RESETS did. The ':fx' key-suffix convention
was specifically documented for telling old Free-tier keys apart from
Pro-tier keys (routing to api-free.deepl.com vs api.deepl.com) — it is
NOT confirmed whether new Developer-tier keys also use ':fx' or
route the same way; this app's _deepl_base_url() logic has not been
re-verified against a real Developer-tier key. If you already hold an
old-style Free ':fx' key from before this retirement, DeepL's notice
is about NEW signups — it's unconfirmed here whether an existing key
still works under its original terms; check your own DeepL account
dashboard rather than trust this file on that point specifically.
The free_chars_per_month figure below is kept for backward
compatibility with any reader still on an old-style key, but a fresh
DeepL signup today should mentally read it as 'up to 1,000,000
characters, once, ever' instead.

gemini-3.5-flash.label: Gemini 3.5 Flash
gemini-3.5-flash.note: Own price is unchanged and still GA (no shutdown date announced) — but Google shipped gemini-3.6-flash on 21 Jul 2026 as the new default/cheaper successor (same $1.50 input, $7.50 output). App's model picker (translate-client.js) still only offers 3.5, not 3.6 — that's a separate app-side change, not a rates.json fix. See the gemini-3.6-flash entry below.

gemini-3.6-flash.label: Gemini 3.6 Flash
gemini-3.6-flash.note: Not yet in the app's model picker (translate-client.js) — added here so the rate table is correct if/when it's wired up. Released 21 Jul 2026 as 3.5 Flash's cheaper successor; 17% fewer output tokens for the same task per Google's own benchmarks, on top of the lower per-token output rate.

gemini-3.1-flash-lite.label: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite
gemini-3.1-flash-lite.note: App's UI currently only offers this on the free tier (see freeTierModels in translate-client.js), so real-world cost is usually $0.00 — these are the standalone paid-tier rates in case that changes.

gemini-2.5-flash.label: Gemini 2.5 Flash
gemini-2.5-flash.note: Google has this retiring 16 Oct 2026 (per ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing) — recheck this entry after that date.

gemini-2.0-flash-lite.label: Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite
gemini-2.0-flash-lite.note: Google shut this model down 1 June 2026. It's still referenced as the /vision-crop default in server.py — flagged separately, not fixed here. Kept in this table so cost tracking doesn't silently misprice any in-flight requests still using it.

deepl.label: DeepL
deepl.note: STALE — see this file's header comment for the full 2026-08-02 correction. This $5.49/1M-chars flat rate describes the RETIRED API Pro plan. DeepL's current paid tier (Growth) doesn't bill this way at all — it's a ~$26/month base fee with 50,000,000 characters/month included, then overage per extra million above that (approx $27.50/1M per third-party trackers, NOT independently confirmed against DeepL's own pricing page — a base-fee-plus-included-allowance plan can't be represented as a single per_million_chars figure the way this field currently assumes, since a Growth user's real cost is usually just the flat $26/month, not the per-character math _deepLCost() computes). This app's cost tracker will OVER-estimate a Growth user's true cost, since it always applies the pure per-character math below regardless of whether the $26/month base already covers everything sent this month. free_chars_per_month=500000 describes the retired Free plan; the current free tier (Developer) is 1,000,000 characters TOTAL, one-time, never resets — not a monthly figure at all. Needs a real fix (a new plan shape, not just an updated number) once Growth's exact current pricing is independently confirmed.
